subject.title: Codex-OAuth models fail over incorrectly — sibling model with healthy per-model quota still drops to non-codex fallback

question: Should OpenClaw make direct OpenAI Responses a supported Codex-OAuth fallback path by adding Harmony tool-call adaptation, or keep Codex-OAuth turns on Codex app-server and pursue the false 429 upstream?
rationale: Current source proves the blockedModel bookkeeping gap and the missing direct-runtime Harmony adapter, but choosing the permanent runtime owner changes Codex tool-call semantics and provider fallback behavior beyond a narrow cleanup.

options.title: Stage bookkeeping, then decide runtime owner
options.body: Review and land or replace the blockedModel PR first, then use live OAuth proof to choose between an OpenClaw direct-runtime adapter and an upstream Codex app-server fix.

options.title: Support direct Codex-OAuth in OpenClaw
options.body: Add Harmony tool-call adaptation to the direct OpenAI Responses runtime and prove Codex-OAuth tools work without the app-server fallback path.

options.title: Keep Codex app-server authoritative
options.body: Treat direct runtime as unsupported for Codex-OAuth tool calls and investigate the sibling-model 429 in upstream Codex or app-server connection/session handling.

recommendation.title: Stage bookkeeping, then decide runtime owner
recommendation.body: Review and land or replace the blockedModel PR first, then use live OAuth proof to choose between an OpenClaw direct-runtime adapter and an upstream Codex app-server fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The highest-confidence current OpenClaw evidence is in the WHAM/auth-profile usage path this owner recently maintained; the final runtime direction may still need adjacent Codex runtime input.
